subject: Queued denial: sudden 429/latency spikes — rate limit config snafu
messages:
From: PulseLeap Ops <ops@pulseleap.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 02:14:00 -0800
Subject: High 429s and latency for /v1/generate — urgent

Sean —

We started seeing a spike in 429s and per-request latency for our production tenant around 01:45 PT. Traffic volume hasn't changed on our side; the pattern looks like short bursts (10–30s) followed by a ~2m period of near-total denial (429s). Our customers are seeing timeouts and page-level errors.

Attached are a 30s sample of client-side error logs and timing traces (pulseleap_429_samples_20261119.log). Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side? We need ETA on mitigation — this is impacting our enterprise customers.

Thanks,
Jenna Park
CFO / Head of Ops
PulseLeap

---
Note: We attempted retries and backoff on our end; behavior persists.
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: PulseLeap Ops <ops@pulseleap.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 02:26:02 -0800
Subject: Re: High 429s and latency for /v1/generate — urgent

Jenna —

Thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. We're treating this as a P1. I've looped in Karthik (infra) and Marissa (SRE lead).

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether these bursts are coming from a small set of API keys or broadly across your tenant? Any recent traffic pattern changes (campaigns, new clients) would help.

We'll push a short mitigation plan as soon as we have root cause. I'll keep you updated every 15 minutes.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the severity.

—Sean
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 03:02:15 -0800
Subject: RE: High 429s and latency for /v1/generate — urgent

Quick technical summary from infra diagnostics (initial):
- Observed symptom: repeated token-bucket exhaustion on the service-tier rate limiter for the PulseLeap tenant; the limiter returns 429s and clips requests, which in turn increases client-side latency and retries.
- Root cause (probable): a recent rollout to the rate-limiter service (commit f3a9b2) introduced a change in how burst credits are refilled after a long idle period. The new refiller uses a per-window cap that does not allow refilling until the tenant's in-flight counter falls below a threshold — this is working as coded but interacts badly with PulseLeap's traffic pattern (tight microbursts). The net effect: bursts consume all credits and the refill path is starved for ~90–150s until the in-flight counter drops.
- Corroborating evidence: matched timestamps between token-bucket drain events and the 429 clusters in the supplied log; rate-limiter logs show "burst_refill_blocked_by_inflight_threshold" entries.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (deploy within next 10–30m):
1) Temporary emergency toggle: enable per-tenant burst-refill-backoff override (config: rate/tenant/override/pulseleap=true) — will allow immediate refill at a safe baseline rate.
2) Route PulseLeap traffic to a dedicated capacity pool for the next 2h to isolate them from global quota behavior.
3) Enable a soft-fallback model for their heavy requests (reduce max_tokens and model variant) to smooth token consumption while the refill behavior is adjusted.

I'll open INF-7831 and push a hotfix to loosen the inflight threshold logic; that fix will need canary validation.

Attachments: sample limiter trace (attached to ticket), emergency_override_playbook_v1.docx (playbook).

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Exec-Risk <exec-risk@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 03:28:40 -0800
Subject: Exec heads-up: PulseLeap production blockage requiring immediate config override

Team —

Summary: PulseLeap (enterprise customer) is experiencing repeated 429s and elevated tail latency due to burst-credit starvation triggered by a recent rate-limiter refactor (commit f3a9b2). This is customer-facing and impacting SLAs. Karthik has identified a safe short-term mitigation (per-tenant burst-refill override + routing to dedicated pool) which requires ops privileges for a live toggle and temporary capacity allocation.

Impact: Several enterprise customers downstream are throwing errors; PulseLeap reports revenue-impacting incidents. We're seeing ~600 429s/min during peak clusters and 4–8s p95 response times during retry storms.

Ask: Approval to apply emergency override for PulseLeap and provision a dedicated capacity slice for 2 hours. This will have marginal cost impact but prevents revenue loss and escalations. Please reply all with +1 to proceed. If I don't get an objection in 5 minutes, I'll authorize ops to apply the toggle.

Sean
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: PulseLeap Ops <ops@pulseleap.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 05:08:12 -0800
Subject: Re: High 429s and latency for /v1/generate — urgent

Jenna —

Thank you for the quick report and logs. We’ve identified a configuration interaction in our rate-limiter that caused burst credits to be starved for tenants with tight microburst patterns (your trace matches the pattern).

What we did (in the last 30m):
- Enabled emergency per-tenant refill override for PulseLeap (rate/tenant/override/pulseleap=true). This immediately allowed the token-bucket to refill and reduced 429s.
- Moved PulseLeap traffic to a dedicated capacity pool for 2 hours to isolate them while we validate the fix.
- Enabled a soft-fallback on high-cost requests for 30 minutes (lowered max_tokens for heavy endpoints) to smooth peak load.

Next steps and ETA:
- Karthik is preparing a hotfix to the refill logic (INF-7831); canary validation starts in 40 minutes. Expect a stable fix and rollback of the override by EOD PST if canary is green.
- We’ll follow up with a postmortem and a permanent policy change to avoid inflight-threshold starvation for bursty tenants.

We sincerely apologize for the outage. Our priority was to restore traffic and reduce customer impact. We’ll keep providing updates in INF-7831 and I’ll ping you with confirmation once the canary completes.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
